subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: A teacher records the minutes 9 students spent on a review quiz: 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, and 41. The class is deciding whether the 41-minute value is typical or unusual.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Identify the median of the data set.
Describe the shape of the distribution and identify whether there is a potential outlier.
Calculate the mean of the data set and state whether the mean is greater than or less than the median.
Explain how removing the 41-minute value would affect the mean and the standard deviation.

criteria.learner_facing_text: States the median is 22 minutes.
Describes the distribution as right-skewed and identifies 41 as a potential outlier.
Computes the mean as about 21.4 minutes and says the mean is less than the median.
Explains that removing 41 lowers the mean and decreases the standard deviation.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: Two classes took different quizzes. On Quiz A, the class mean was 74 and the standard deviation was 8. On Quiz B, the class mean was 52 and the standard deviation was 4. A student scored 86 on Quiz A and 62 on Quiz B.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Calculate the student's z-score on Quiz A.
Calculate the student's z-score on Quiz B.
Determine on which quiz the student performed better relative to the class.
Explain why z-scores are useful for comparing scores from different quizzes.

criteria.learner_facing_text: Computes the Quiz A z-score as 1.5.
Computes the Quiz B z-score as 2.5.
States that the student performed better relative to the class on Quiz B.
Explains that z-scores place scores on a common scale measured in standard deviations from the mean.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: A tutor tracked the number of hours students studied for a practice test and the scores they earned. The least-squares regression line for the data is y-hat = 52 + 4.1x, where x is study hours and y is test score. The correlation is r = 0.93.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Interpret the slope of the regression line in context.
Describe the direction and strength of the association.
Predict the score for a student who studied for 6 hours.
If the observed score for that student was 74, calculate the residual and interpret its sign.

criteria.learner_facing_text: States that each additional study hour is associated with about 4.1 more test points on average.
Describes the relationship as strong and positive.
Computes the prediction as 76.6.
Computes the residual as -2.6 and explains that the observed score is 2.6 points below the predicted value.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: A regression study on screen time and sleep used data from students whose screen time ranged from 1 to 8 hours per day. The regression line is y-hat = 9.8 - 0.65x, where y is hours of sleep. A student who used screens for 7 hours slept 5.0 hours.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Interpret the slope in context.
Predict the sleep time for a student with 7 hours of screen time.
Calculate the residual for the 7-hour student.
Explain why using the line to predict sleep for 12 hours of screen time would be extrapolation.

criteria.learner_facing_text: States that each additional hour of screen time is associated with about 0.65 fewer hours of sleep on average.
Computes the prediction as 5.25 hours of sleep.
Computes the residual as -0.25 hours and recognizes the student slept less than predicted.
Explains that 12 hours is outside the observed x-range of 1 to 8 hours.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: A school newspaper wants to estimate the proportion of students who support a later start time. Reporters stand outside the cafeteria at lunch and ask the first 50 students who agree to answer.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Identify the sampling method used.
Describe one source of bias in the sample.
Explain how a simple random sample of 50 students could be selected instead.
Explain why the results should not be generalized to all students without caution.

criteria.learner_facing_text: Identifies the method as a convenience sample or voluntary response sample.
Describes undercoverage or self-selection bias from only surveying students at lunch who agree to respond.
Explains that all students should be put in a list and 50 should be chosen randomly.
Explains that the sample may not represent the whole student body because of the selection method.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: A researcher wants to study whether a 10-minute mindfulness app lowers quiz anxiety. Sixty volunteers are available. The researcher records each student's baseline anxiety score before the study.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Identify the explanatory variable and the response variable.
Explain why random assignment is needed in this study.
Describe how the baseline anxiety scores could be used to create blocks.
State whether this should be described as an experiment or an observational study, and justify your answer.

criteria.learner_facing_text: Names app use as the explanatory variable and post-treatment quiz anxiety as the response variable.
Explains that random assignment helps reduce confounding and supports a cause-and-effect conclusion.
Describes grouping students by similar baseline anxiety levels before random assignment.
Identifies the study as an experiment because the researcher assigns the treatment.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: A student answers 20 multiple-choice questions on a practice test. Each question has four choices, and the student guesses on every question. The chance of a correct guess on any question is 0.25, and the guesses are independent.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Explain why the number of correct answers can be modeled with a binomial random variable.
Calculate the mean number of correct answers.
Calculate the standard deviation of the number of correct answers.
Approximate the probability of getting exactly 5 questions correct.

criteria.learner_facing_text: States fixed n, two outcomes per question, independent trials, and constant p = 0.25.
Computes the mean as 5 correct answers.
Computes the standard deviation as about 1.94.
Computes P(X = 5) as about 0.202.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: A school fundraiser sells a raffle ticket with the following payoff X: with probability 0.20 the buyer wins 10 dollars, with probability 0.50 the buyer wins 2 dollars, and with probability 0.30 the buyer loses 4 dollars. The payout is the buyer's net gain in dollars.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Calculate the expected value of X.
Calculate the standard deviation of X.
Interpret the expected value in context.
Explain why a positive expected value does not guarantee that one buyer will make money on a single ticket.

criteria.learner_facing_text: Computes the expected value as 3.2 dollars.
Computes the standard deviation as about 5.0 dollars.
Explains that the long-run average net gain per ticket is about 3.20 dollars.
Explains that expected value describes many repetitions, not the outcome of one ticket purchase.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: In a large school district, the true proportion of students who own a bicycle is believed to be p = 0.28. A simple random sample of 400 students is selected and the sample proportion p-hat is recorded.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Find the mean of the sampling distribution of p-hat.
Find the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of p-hat.
Explain why a normal model is reasonable for p-hat in this setting.
Explain how the standard deviation would change if the sample size were doubled.

criteria.learner_facing_text: States that the mean of the sampling distribution is 0.28.
Computes the standard deviation as about 0.0225.
Explains that np and n(1-p) are both at least 10.
Explains that doubling n would reduce the standard deviation because it is divided by the square root of n.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: The distribution of the number of hours students sleep on a school night has mean mu = 7.2 hours and standard deviation sigma = 1.8 hours. A simple random sample of 36 students is selected and the sample mean x-bar is recorded.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Find the mean of the sampling distribution of x-bar.
Find the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of x-bar.
Explain why the sampling distribution of x-bar is approximately normal.
Explain how the standard deviation would change if the sample size were reduced to 9.

criteria.learner_facing_text: States that the mean of the sampling distribution is 7.2 hours.
Computes the standard deviation as 0.3 hours.
Explains that the sample size is large enough for the CLT to apply.
Explains that the standard deviation would increase to 0.6 hours because the sample size is smaller.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: A school surveys 120 students about whether they support a later start time. Eighty-four students say yes.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: State the parameter of interest and calculate p-hat.
Check the conditions for a one-proportion confidence interval.
Calculate a 95% confidence interval for the proportion of all students who support a later start time.
Interpret the interval in context.

criteria.learner_facing_text: Identifies the parameter as the true proportion of all students who support a later start time and computes p-hat = 0.70.
Checks randomization/independence and success-failure conditions using 84 and 36.
Computes an interval of about (0.618, 0.782).
Interprets the interval as a range of plausible values for the true population proportion of supportive students.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: A principal claims that more than half of students prefer digital homework reminders. In a random sample of 100 students, 62 say they prefer digital reminders.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Write the null and alternative hypotheses.
Calculate the test statistic for a one-proportion z test.
Find the approximate p-value and state the decision at alpha = 0.05.
State the conclusion in context.

criteria.learner_facing_text: States H0: p = 0.50 and Ha: p > 0.50.
Computes z as about 2.40.
Gives a p-value about 0.008 and rejects H0 at alpha = 0.05.
Concludes that there is convincing evidence that more than half of students prefer digital homework reminders.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: A sample of 16 students has a mean sleep time of 74 minutes during a study hall and a sample standard deviation of 8 minutes. A teacher wants to know whether the true mean sleep time is 70 minutes.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Write the null and alternative hypotheses.
Calculate the t test statistic.
Calculate a 95% confidence interval for the true mean sleep time.
Interpret the interval in context.

criteria.learner_facing_text: States H0: mu = 70 and Ha: mu != 70.
Computes t as 2.00 using x-bar = 74, mu0 = 70, s = 8, and n = 16.
Computes a 95% interval of about (69.7, 78.3).
Interprets the interval as a plausible range for the true mean sleep time for the population of students.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: A teacher tests a practice program by giving 25 students a pretest and a posttest. The differences defined as posttest minus pretest have mean 4.2 points and standard deviation 3.0 points.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Explain why this should be analyzed with paired data.
Calculate the t statistic for testing whether the mean difference is 0.
State the approximate p-value decision if the test is conducted at alpha = 0.05.
State the conclusion in context.

criteria.learner_facing_text: Explains that each student's pretest and posttest scores are matched, so the analysis uses differences within students.
Computes t as about 7.00.
States that the p-value is very small and rejects H0 at alpha = 0.05.
Concludes that the program appears to increase scores for the population of similar students.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: A spinner is supposed to be fair across four colors. After 100 spins, the observed counts are 18 red, 27 blue, 25 green, and 30 yellow.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Write the null and alternative hypotheses for a chi-square goodness-of-fit test.
Calculate the expected count in each color category.
Calculate the chi-square test statistic.
State the conclusion at alpha = 0.05.

criteria.learner_facing_text: States H0: all four colors are equally likely and Ha: the distribution is not equal across the four colors.
States that the expected count is 25 for each color.
Computes chi-square as 3.12.
Fails to reject H0 at alpha = 0.05 and explains that the data do not give convincing evidence the spinner is unfair.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus:
A school wants to know whether grade level and preference for a new app are independent. The observed counts are:

|           | Likes app | Does not like app |
|-----------|-----------|-------------------|
| Freshman  | 18        | 12                |
| Sophomore | 12        | 18                |
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Write the null and alternative hypotheses for a chi-square test of independence.
Calculate the expected count for freshmen who like the app.
Calculate the chi-square test statistic.
State the conclusion at alpha = 0.05.

criteria.learner_facing_text: States H0: grade level and app preference are independent and Ha: they are associated.
Computes the expected count for freshmen who like the app as 15.
Computes chi-square as 2.40.
Fails to reject H0 at alpha = 0.05 and explains that there is not convincing evidence of an association.

subject: AP Statistics
stimulus: A regression analysis of test score y on study hours x uses n = 18 students. The slope estimate is b = 5.2 and the standard error of the slope is 1.1.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Write the null and alternative hypotheses for the slope.
Calculate the t statistic for testing the slope.
State the approximate p-value decision at alpha = 0.05.
Interpret the slope in context.

criteria.learner_facing_text: States H0: beta1 = 0 and Ha: beta1 != 0.
Computes t as about 4.73.
States that the p-value is very small and rejects H0 at alpha = 0.05.
Explains that each additional study hour is associated with about 5.2 more test points on average.

subject: AP Statistics
subtopics: 9.2 Confidence Interval for a Regression Slope
stimulus: A study models exercise minutes x and resting heart rate y for 22 adults. The least-squares slope is b = -2.4 beats per minute per exercise minute, and the standard error of the slope is 0.6. The study only collected exercise times from 0 to 30 minutes.
stem: Answer all parts of the following question.

parts.prompt_text: Calculate a 95% confidence interval for the true slope.
Interpret the interval in context.
Explain why the interval should not be used to predict heart rate for 50 minutes of exercise.
State whether the confidence interval suggests a negative, positive, or zero slope.

criteria.learner_facing_text: Computes a 95% confidence interval of about (-3.65, -1.15).
Explains that the true slope is plausibly between about -3.65 and -1.15 beats per minute per exercise minute.
Explains that 50 minutes is outside the observed x-range, so using the model there would be extrapolation.
States that the interval suggests a negative slope because the entire interval is below 0.
